name: webpack
summary: A configurable JavaScript module compiler that builds a module graph through loaders and plugins, derives chunk graphs during compilation, and emits runtime-specific assets with caching and watch support.

features.name: Compiler and compilation lifecycle
features.description: The fixed source separates Compiler orchestration from Compilation state and exposes lifecycle hooks for module building, optimization, asset processing, sealing, and emission. Plugins attach to these hooks through the compiler and compilation objects.
benefits: Makes build phases and extension points observable
Allows plugins to coordinate work around a shared compilation state
costs: Phase ordering and hook timing constrain plugin correctness
Large compilation state increases memory and lifecycle management cost

features.name: Module and chunk graph compilation
features.description: Compilation owns ModuleGraph and ChunkGraph structures that relate module dependencies, chunks, chunk groups, runtimes, and entrypoints. The compiler can therefore derive output groupings from a dependency graph rather than treating each input file as an isolated asset.
benefits: Supports code splitting, shared chunks, and runtime-aware output
Makes dependency and chunk relationships available to optimization passes
costs: Graph optimization and chunk assignment add build-time computation
Dynamic loading and runtime targets create multiple output constraints

features.name: Loader and plugin extension surface
features.description: Webpack resolves module requests through configured loaders and applies plugins through Tapable compiler and compilation hooks. Loaders transform resource content while plugins can observe or change broad compilation phases.
benefits: Accommodates non-JavaScript resources and framework-specific transforms
Enables optimization, reporting, and output customization without editing the compiler core
costs: Configuration and hook ordering become part of the effective architecture
A loader or plugin can alter graph semantics and complicate debugging

features.name: Asset, cache, and emission boundary
features.description: The fixed compiler and compilation sources include asset processing hooks and filesystem/cache support around build results. Webpack can retain build information for later runs while emitting target-specific assets and runtime code.
benefits: Improves repeat-build performance and supports deployment-specific assets
Separates intermediate compilation state from emitted files
costs: Cache invalidation and serialization must reflect loader, plugin, and filesystem changes
Runtime-specific output and asset processing increase configuration surface

mathematical_views.question: How does a webpack compilation transition from configured inputs through graph construction, optimization, asset processing, and emission?
assumptions: Compiler hooks define ordered lifecycle phases
Compilation state is the subject of phase transitions
The view abstracts individual loader implementations and filesystem scheduling

mathematical_views.question: How are module dependency edges transformed into chunks, chunk groups, entrypoints, and runtime-aware outputs?
assumptions: Modules and chunks are graph nodes with explicit dependency and membership edges
Chunk assignment is a compilation transformation rather than a claim about runtime network behavior
Dynamic import semantics and target runtime code are abstracted

mathematical_views.question: Which loader and plugin transformations preserve enough module and asset metadata for later compiler phases?
assumptions: Loaders produce transformed module inputs and plugins observe phase hooks
Hook composition is modeled as a candidate algebra over compilation state
Arbitrary third-party plugin compatibility remains an empirical validation question

benefits: Explicit phases support broad build customization
costs: Hook timing and shared mutable state raise coordination cost

benefits: Powerful code splitting and runtime-aware optimization
costs: Graph construction and optimization increase build complexity
Configuration and extension interactions can obscure failure causes
Cache invalidation and serialized state require careful provenance

relations.notes: The reviewed webpack compiler/plugin surface is a JavaScript implementation and its official documentation shows Node.js core-module use in webpack configuration; a runtime-specific edge is proposed pending a direct package-runtime evidence item.
